source_resources.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
source_resources.author: Noah Shinn, Federico Cassano, Ashwin Gopinath, Karthik Narasimhan, Shunyu Yao
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external academic reference under open access repository terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Reinforcement learning concepts, agent evaluation loops, and error feedback handling.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Rigorous framework analyzing dynamic error feedback, memory buffering of execution failures, and controlled self-reflection loops without updating model weights.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Error recovery state diagrams and retry budget algorithms are detailed in curriculum materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback (Madaan et al. 2023)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Single-turn generative text refinement; Reflexion operates across multi-turn external environment action-observation failures.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Ghost in the Minecraft: Generally Capable Agents for Open-World Environments via Large Language Models with Text-based Knowledge and Memory (Zhu et al. 2023)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Domain-specific LLM-based agent for open-world Minecraft; Reflexion establishes domain-general verbal feedback control loops.

source_resources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
source_resources.author: Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan, Yuan Cao
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external technical citation and reference under open access repository terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Prompt engineering, token generation basics, and conversational interaction loops.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational academic paper introducing the interleaved Thought-Action-Observation control loop in LLM agents, establishing formal interleaving of task reasoning and external tool execution.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Permanently accessible on arXiv.org open access repository.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete algorithmic step traces, state loop diagrams, and control loop pseudocode are self-contained in curriculum materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models (Wei et al. 2022)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Pure reasoning without environmental actions or external tool grounding; ReAct extends reasoning into an interactive environment action-observation loop.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: MRKL Systems: A modular, neuro-symbolic architecture that combines large language models, external knowledge sources and discrete reasoning (Karpas et al. 2022)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Early neuro-symbolic modular router concept; ReAct offers simpler, prompting-native action-observation loop dynamics suitable for standard API models.

source_resources.title: RFC 8259: The JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) Data Interchange Format
source_resources.author: Tim Bray (Ed.)
source_resources.prerequisites: Text encoding, UTF-8 parsing, and serialized data exchange.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational Internet standard defining strict JSON grammar, token parsing, and whitespace rules underpinning model tool calling serialization.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publicly accessible permanently via RFC Editor repository.
source_resources.safe_fallback: JSON grammar parsing rules and error recovery guidelines are documented in curriculum notes.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Binary serialization standard; text-based LLMs operate primarily on human-readable UTF-8 JSON interchange formats.
Indentation-sensitive text format; JSON has universally standardized parsing across language runtimes and tool schemas.

source_resources.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Specification
source_resources.author: Anthropic PBC & Open Source Contributors
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Architecture Overview, Transports, Tools, and Resources
source_resources.license: Apache-2.0 (specification; unrelicensed legacy contributions remain MIT) / Open Specification
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful open protocol documentation and architecture specification under Apache-2.0 (legacy contributions under MIT).
source_resources.prerequisites: Client-server architecture, JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol, and standard IO communication.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Normative open architecture specification defining Host, Client, and Server separation, resource subscriptions, tool listing/invoking primitives, and JSON-RPC 2.0 message framing.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publicly hosted on modelcontextprotocol.io and GitHub repository.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Architectural comparison tables, loop invariants, and message frame examples are self-contained in curriculum materials.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Precursor JSON-RPC architecture for code intelligence in IDEs; MCP adapts similar client-server decoupling specifically for LLM context, tools, and prompts.
Hosted, vendor-managed built-in tool execution (successor to the Assistants API tools); MCP provides an open, decoupled local/remote client-server standard.

source_resources.title: Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
source_resources.author: Timo Schick, Jane Dwivedi-Yu, Roberto Dessì, Roberta Raileanu, Maria Lomeli, Luke Zettlemoyer, Nicola Cancedda, Thomas Scialom
source_resources.license: arXiv.org perpetual non-exclusive license / Open Access
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external technical citation and reference under open access repository terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Transformer autoregressive generation, API calling syntax, and self-supervised filtering.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Original paper demonstrating self-supervised discovery and execution of tool API calls (calculator, QA, search, calendar) via inline tokenized tool invocations.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Permanently accessible on arXiv.org open access repository.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Inline tool invocation formats and self-contained mock execution traces are provided in curriculum notes.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Gorilla: Large Language Model Connected with Massive APIs (Patil et al. 2023)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Focuses on massive API retrieval and documentation formatting; Toolformer focuses on the fundamental token-level seam between model generation and tool execution.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: TALM: Tool Augmented Language Models (Parisi et al. 2022)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Iterative search-and-execute augmentation; Toolformer provides clearer self-supervised API call tokenization syntax.
